Subject: SLA draft — uptime targets and credit mechanics

Hi Laura,

Thanks for sending the initial template last week. Our legal and infra teams reviewed it and we have two main questions before we can move to procurement:

1) Uptime floor — our platform is customer-facing and we need at least 99.95% for the inference endpoints used in production.
2) Monthly remedy (service credits) — the draft lists a single credit slab but our finance team wants clearer tiers tied to percentage of monthly spend and a lower cap for pilot months.

I've attached our redlines (Sawbridge_redlines_20250720.docx) with inline feedback. A couple of specific asks from infra: carve out scheduled maintenance windows but not long-running platform work, and add a clause for latency SLO exceptions for batched/throughput-optimized jobs.

Can we set up a quick call later this week, or alternatively provide a written counter-offer on the points above?

Best,
Elliot Reyes
Head of Platform Engineering
Sawbridge Systems

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: SLA draft — uptime targets and credit mechanics

Elliot —

Appreciate the redlines and context. Quick written counter to get this moving:

- Hosted (standard) offering: 99.9% monthly availability with tiered credits.
  - Availability >= 99.9%: no credit
  - 99.5% <= Availability < 99.9%: 5% of monthly invoice
  - 98.0% <= Availability < 99.5%: 15% of monthly invoice
  - Availability < 98.0%: 30% of monthly invoice

- Dedicated (reserved capacity): optional premium addendum for 99.95% at an incremental fee (we can show numbers). If you select Dedicated and pay the uplift, remedy tiers improve: 0% / 3% / 10% / 25% respectively.

- Monthly credit cap: standard is 100% of monthly fees. For pilot months (first two months post-launch) we can agree a temporary cap of 50% to limit early-stage variability; after that standard caps apply.

- Maintenance carveouts: scheduled maintenance (published >= 7 days) is excluded. Urgent maintenance that is communicated with reasonable lead time will be excluded if it follows the notice obligations. For multi-region customers we can align maintenance windows region-by-region.

- Latency exceptions: we can include a negotiated exception for long-running batch inference jobs where latency SLOs are relaxed, but availability counts the endpoint as available unless the control plane reports an outage. We will add language to distinguish throughput-optimized endpoints that may accept higher tail latency.

I've attached a clean copy of our SLA template (Redwood_SLA_v1.pdf) showing where we'd insert the Dedicated addendum and pilot cap language. Happy to hop on a call Thursday afternoon with aditya and grace if that helps.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Director, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

Looping in a short commercial note from the sales side:

- Pricing/commitment tradeoff: Sawbridge can elect Dedicated pools for mission-critical low-latency traffic. We usually price 99.95% as an add-on (~+15-25% of committed monthly for comparable throughput); I can get exact uplift once we understand your regional split and burst profile.

- Credit cap rationale: the 100% monthly cap protects both parties and is industry standard. For high-risk pilots we can agree to a 50% pilot cap, then revisit at renewal.

- Canary/rollout protections: we recommend adding an automatic fallback to a lower-cost hosted variant during capacity events to preserve availability for your core user journeys; that can be called out as an operational remedy rather than a credit.

Elliot — curious about two specifics from your infra redlines: (1) Are all your production inference calls routed through a single endpoint (so a regional split would matter), and (2) do you have batch vs. on-demand traffic clearly segmented? If so, we can propose endpoint-level SLOs.

- Aditya
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
From: Elliot Reyes <elliot.reyes@sawbridge.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: contracts@sawbridge.com
Date: Sun, 20 Jul 2025 08:09:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA draft — uptime targets and credit mechanics

Thanks — answers inline to help speed a final doc:

- Regional split: yes, we run a primary in us-west and a DR region in eu-west. We need the option to have regionally measured availability and corresponding credits (DR traffic is lower criticality, primary is critical).

- Batch segmentation: we have two distinct paths — realtime inference for user-facing requests (high priority) and bulk batch jobs for model retraining & analytics. Batch jobs can tolerate higher P99 latency. We want the contract to reflect that availability/latency SLOs are measured on the realtime endpoints only.

Redlines summary attached — main sticking points: (A) move Dedicated 99.95 into the main SLA as an option rather than a separate addendum, and (B) lower the monthly credit cap for the first live month to 30% not 50%.

Can we converge on a written term sheet? If we can get a mutually acceptable term sheet by end of week, procurement will start the PO process.

Cheers,
Elliot

Elliot / team — thanks for the clear redlines and the fast turnaround. Below is a concise term sheet we can sign to unlock procurement and pricing: please confirm acceptance or provide a single consolidated redline.

Term sheet (high level):
- Measurement and scope: availability measured per-region on realtime inference endpoints. Batch endpoints excluded from realtime availability measurements and will have separate latency guidance in an appendix.
- Hosted (standard): 99.9% monthly availability with credits: 5% (99.5-99.9), 15% (98.0-99.5), 30% (<98.0).
- Dedicated option: selectable at contract execution for 99.95% availability (flat uplift applied to committed capacity). Remedy tiers for Dedicated: 3% / 10% / 25% respectively.
- Monthly credit cap: 100% of monthly fees after the first full billing month. For go-live month we agree a capped pilot remedy of 30% of that month’s fees (per your request).
- Maintenance carveouts: scheduled maintenance (>=7 days notice) excluded. Emergency maintenance limited to documented incident response and communicated promptly.
- Operational remedies: we will provide a runbook for canary rollouts and a documented fallback policy; executing the fallback is considered an operational mitigation and does not waive credit eligibility for an outage but reduces customer impact.
- Latency exceptions: batch/throughput endpoints explicitly excluded from realtime P99 commitments; we will add appendix text to define measurement windows and acceptable tail latency for those endpoints.

Next steps: if Sawbridge confirms the term sheet above, Redwood legal will produce a redlined SLA (single doc including Dedicated option) by EOD Friday and coordinate with your contracts team for a final pass. Aditya will follow up on uplift pricing and regional capacity sizing.

Thanks again — we want to make sure the commercial and operational pieces align so your launch goes smoothly.

Best,
